sections.h2: What does the Fayette County Clerk of Superior Court do in a home sale?
sections.html:
The clerk records the deed that moves a Fayette County house from seller to buyer, along with mortgages, releases, liens and plats. The office describes itself as the keeper of public records for the county, and Georgia has made the clerk a constitutional officer since the 1798 constitution.

The clerk also serves State and Magistrate Courts and, since July 1, 2010, runs the clerical side of the county Board of Equalization, which hears property tax valuation disputes. For a seller that means one address matters twice: the deed and any recorded lien come through here, and so does the paperwork if a valuation appeal reaches the equalization board.

Fayette County was set up in 1821 as Georgia's 49th county, covers about 199 square miles south of Atlanta, and borders Fulton, Clayton, Spalding and Coweta counties. Deeds for property in Fayetteville, Peachtree City, Tyrone, Brooks, Woolsey and the unincorporated areas all record with this one clerk.

sections.h2: Where is the Fayette County clerk's office and when can I look at records?
sections.html:
The clerk is at One Center Drive, Fayetteville, GA 30214, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 130. The main line is 770-716-4290, and the county's page lists 770-716-4291 for the Real Estate division.

Public records can be inspected from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, except official holidays. The clerk's search policy says deeds, liens and similar non-court papers are open to inspection under the Georgia Open Records Act, so no formal open records request is needed to look at them during those hours. Public computer terminals inside the office show images without staff supervision.

  • Property index search is on the clerk's Online Services page.
  • A property and mortgage fraud check alerts you when something is recorded against a registered parcel.
  • The court docket search covers Superior, State and Magistrate Courts.

Register a parcel with the fraud alert if you own a vacant or inherited house in Fayette, since a forged deed or an odd lien is easier to fix when you see it early.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed or release in Fayette County?
sections.html:
The clerk's court fee schedule, revised July 1, 2024, charges a flat fee for real estate filings. The figures below come straight from that schedule, so check the current sheet before you bring a check.

Selected Fayette County clerk fees (court fee schedule revised July 1, 2024)
Filing or serviceFee
Recording a document pertaining to real estate$25.00
Cancellation, satisfaction, release or assignment, each instrument listed$25.00
Plat, map or floor plan, each page$10.00
Lien, lis pendens, notice or bond$25.00
Tax lien by a state or local government agency$5.00
Certified copy of a document, per page$0.50
Each certification or exemplification with seal$2.50
Veteran's discharge record, valid identification requiredNo fee

The same schedule lists uncertified copies at $0.50 a page when you copy them yourself and $1.00 a page with staff help. For a certified copy of a deed, the clerk points people to the eCertification site at ecert.gsccca.org, and regular copies requested by email run $1.00 per page with payment in advance.

sections.h2: Can I file a Fayette County deed electronically?
sections.html:
Yes, and for many documents electronic filing is now the expected route. The Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority writes in its real property guidelines that, with some exceptions, since January 1, 2025 deeds, liens, plats and other real property documents in electronic form are to be filed through the Authority's eFiling Portal. Paper documents go directly to the clerk.

The Fayette clerk's Online Services page links to eFiling for real estate and UCC documents through the Authority. Most sellers never touch it, since the attorney or title company running the closing e-records the deed. If you are handling a family transfer without a closing firm, ask the clerk's Real Estate division at 770-716-4291 whether a paper filing is accepted for your document before you drive over.

The Authority's filing page also says electronic filing is offered in participating counties, so a county's participation is a local decision. Confirm Fayette's current rules with the clerk before relying on either route.

sections.h2: What is the Georgia transfer tax and the PT-61 form in Fayette County?
sections.html:
Georgia requires the real estate transfer tax to be paid before a deed can be recorded with the clerk, and the clerk then attaches a certification that the tax was paid. The Department of Revenue prints the rate as $1 for the first $1,000 of the sale price and 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part of $100, under O.C.G.A. 48-6-1 through 48-6-10.

The seller is the party liable, though a contract often shifts it to the buyer. For questions about exemptions, the Department of Revenue tells people to ask the clerk of superior court in the county.

The PT-61 declaration is filled out online through the Clerks' Authority. After you finish, print a copy to file with the deed, and file only one PT-61 for each applicable deed. The Authority's customer support line, listed on the Department of Revenue page, is (800) 304-5174.

sections.h2: What recording rules apply to a mortgage payoff or intangible tax in Fayette County?
sections.html:
When a lender is paid off, the release or cancellation of its security deed is recorded with the clerk, and the schedule above lists $25.00 per instrument. Ask your closing attorney to confirm that the release for your old loan is filed, because an open loan can resurface in a later buyer's title search.

A long-term note secured by real estate also carries an intangible recording tax. The state describes it as $1.50 for each $500 of the note's face amount, with the security instrument recorded within 90 days. The Department of Revenue says the clerk collects it in most counties and the tax commissioner in others, so ask the Fayette clerk whether this applies to your transaction.

The clerk's schedule lists a veteran's discharge record as no fee when valid identification is shown.

sections.h2: What housing numbers frame a Fayette County sale?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau puts Fayette County's population at 125,156 for July 1, 2025. Housing facts from the 2020 to 2024 survey show a market that leans heavily toward owners.

  • Owner-occupied rate: 80.1 percent.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $436,400.
  • Median gross rent: $1,898 a month.
  • Median household income: $111,978.
  • Adults 25 and older with a bachelor's degree or more: 49.9 percent.
  • Mean commute: 31.4 minutes.
  • Building permits in 2025: 435.

At those values, even the flat $25.00 recording fee is a small part of a sale, and the transfer tax is the larger recording cost. The county says interstates 75, 85 and 285 are within reach and that MARTA service runs from nearby Fulton County, which matters to commuters who buy here.

faqs.q: How much does the Fayette County clerk charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: The clerk's fee schedule, revised July 1, 2024, lists $25.00 for recording a document pertaining to real estate. Releases and satisfactions are $25.00 per instrument listed, and plats are $10.00 a page.

faqs.q: Who pays the Georgia transfer tax on a Fayette County sale?
faqs.a: The seller is liable by law, though many contracts make the buyer pay it. The tax must be paid before the clerk records the deed, and it is figured from the sale price under the rate the Department of Revenue prints.

faqs.q: Where is the Fayette County Clerk of Superior Court?
faqs.a: The office is at One Center Drive in Fayetteville, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 130, Fayetteville, GA 30214. Call 770-716-4290, or 770-716-4291 for the Real Estate division.

faqs.q: Can I look at a recorded Fayette County deed without a formal request?
faqs.a: Yes. The clerk's search policy says deeds and similar records are open to the public under Georgia's Open Records Act, so you can inspect them from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays without filing an open records request.

faqs.q: Does the Fayette County clerk also handle property tax appeals?
faqs.a: The clerk manages the county Board of Equalization's records, notices and hearings, but valuation appeals start with the Board of Tax Assessors. After a hearing, the equalization board's decision can go to Superior Court.
